extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency NEPA practitioners, environmental attorneys, Tribal governments, and public stakeholders involved in NEPA reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for agencies on drafting, scheduling, tiering, incorporating materials into, and publicly disclosing Environmental Assessments (EAs), Environmental Impact Statements (EISs), and programmatic NEPA documents consistent with revised CEQ regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of delay (scheduling factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ interprets 'consequences of delay' to include any cost-related consequences to the public of short- or long-term delays; paragraph (d)(1) also covers potential for environmental harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider both environmental harm and cost-related public consequences when developing schedules; CEQ treats 'consequences of delay' broadly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial dispute (replacement of 'controversial')
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory language replaces 'controversial' with 'substantial dispute' consistent with case law distinguishing scientific disputes over size, nature, or effect of an action from mere public opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ views the change as consistent with precedent (e.g., Bark v. U.S. Forest Serv.; Native Ecosystems Council; Standing Rock) and declines to retain 'controversial' to avoid confusion with general public controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for government-to-government Tribal consultation (scheduling factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider the time necessary to conduct government-to-government Tribal consultation when building NEPA schedules; CEQ adds paragraph (d)(9) to encourage inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While agencies can already account for consultation time, CEQ adds this factor to encourage agencies to build sufficient schedule time for meaningful consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-ordered deadlines (scheduling factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should include court-ordered deadlines among time limits imposed on the agency when developing schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds 'court ordered deadlines' to paragraph (d)(8) because some NEPA actions are subject to court orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS schedules must list specific minimum milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: EIS schedules must include at minimum: publication of the NOI, issuance of the draft EIS, the public comment period, issuance of the final EIS, and issuance of the ROD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ redesignates provisions to require these milestones (proposed §1501.10(e)); list is non-exhaustive and agencies may include additional milestones or follow future CEQ guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA schedules must list minimum milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedules for EAs must identify: the decision to prepare an EA; issuance of a draft EA, where applicable; the public comment period, where applicable; and issuance of the final EA and a decision whether to issue a FONSI or NOI to prepare an EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds paragraphs (f)(1)-(f)(4) to identify these milestones; agencies may include additional milestones on an action-by-action basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of EIS schedules and revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to make schedules for EISs publicly available and to publish revisions to the schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds paragraph (h) to increase predictability and accountability; revisions should be published and include explanation for substantial revisions to aid transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation required for substantial schedule revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When agencies publish revisions to an EIS schedule, they must include an explanation for substantial revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declines to define 'substantial' in the rule, deferring to agencies to determine what changes are substantial based on complexity and context; CEQ may issue guidance later.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA schedule posting encouraged but not required
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ encourages agencies to make EA schedules publicly available, especially when it would facilitate public engagement, but does not require publication for all EAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ is concerned that requiring posting of all EA schedules could increase administrative burden since many EAs have simple schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of agency discretion to designate an expediter
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (g) allows an agency to designate a person to expedite the NEPA process; CEQ declines to add further requirements on when or who should fill the role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retains longstanding flexibility from the 1978 regulations for agencies to assign staff to expedite processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of public request mechanism for setting time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ removes the provision allowing State, Tribal, or local agencies, or members of the public to request a Federal agency set time limits because statutory deadlines in section 107(g) render it unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ notes that State/Tribal/local agencies still have roles (joint lead/cooperating/participating) in schedule development but the statutory scheme governs time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling supplementation and effects on timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency determines a supplemental draft EA or EIS is necessary, the end point remains the final EA or final EIS; the lead agency may extend the deadline under §1501.10(b) to complete the final document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For supplemental EAs/EISs prepared after completion of a final document, the lead agency should develop schedules for the supplemental review consistent with §1501.10(b) and section 107(g) of NEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic environmental documents are permitted but not mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may prepare programmatic EAs or EISs to evaluate environmental effects of policies, programs, plans, or groups of related activities; CEQ declines to require programmatic documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic documents are 'best practice' for broad Federal actions (programs, policies, rulemakings, series of projects) and should be timely and relevant to agency planning and decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic documents should be relevant and timed to meaningful planning points
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic environmental documents should be relevant to the agency's decisions and timed to coincide with meaningful points in agency planning and decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised wording to emphasize relevance and timing and broadened 'program' to 'agency' and 'statements' to 'documents' to include EAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic documents must identify anticipated decisions relying on them
rubrics_metrics.description: A programmatic document must identify any decisions or categories of decisions that the agency anticipates making in reliance on it, including actions the agency anticipates making without additional analysis and actions anticipated to be made after a subsequent tiered document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures transparency about the relationship between programmatic and subsequent documents; agencies are not required to list every conceivable circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping, tiering, and other efficiency tools recommended (should not shall)
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ recommends agencies employ scoping, tiering, and other tools to describe relationships between programmatic documents and related actions to reduce duplication; language uses 'should' rather than 'shall'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping is required for EISs but not EAs; requiring tiering for all programmatic documents would be unduly constraining given uncertainty early in planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiering may be used with EISs, EAs, or programmatic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may employ tiering with an EIS, EA, or programmatic environmental document relevant to a later proposed action to avoid duplication and focus on issues, effects, or alternatives not fully addressed earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarifies and reorders references to EISs, EAs, and programmatic documents for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered documents must discuss relationship to earlier review, analyze site-specific conditions, and provide public engagement opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Tiered documents must discuss the relationship between the tiered analysis and the previous review; analyze site-, phase-, or stage-specific conditions and effects; and allow for public engagement opportunities appropriate to the document type and location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tiered document must state where the earlier document is publicly available; tiering does not relieve agencies of requirements for alternatives or public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiering cannot be used to circumvent NEPA requirements (alternatives, hard look, public review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies cannot use programmatic documents or tiering to avoid NEPA requirements, including the obligation to consider a reasonable range of alternatives or to provide opportunities for public comment and site-specific 'hard looks.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ rejects concerns that tiering or programmatic CEs could limit consideration of alternatives; agencies must comply with requirements applicable to EAs or EISs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiently detailed programmatic analyses may allow reliance with little or no additional review
rubrics_metrics.description: A sufficiently detailed programmatic analysis with project descriptions can allow agencies to rely upon programmatic environmental documents for further actions with no or little additional environmental review necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should provide descriptions of planned activities and engage the public throughout the NEPA process, and consider re-engagement before implementation when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reevaluation requirement for programmatic documents older than five years
rubrics_metrics.description: When relying on programmatic environmental documents older than five years, agencies are required to briefly document their reevaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ will not prescribe detailed steps for reevaluation; agencies may use tiered documents to support reevaluation and reevaluation need not be lengthy if accuracy can be quickly verified; statutory timeframes are controlling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiering during reevaluation and five-year statutory presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 108 allows agencies to tier from a programmatic review in a subsequent environmental document for up to five years without additional analysis; tiered documents relying on the programmatic document during those five years are entitled to the statutory presumption that no additional review is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declines to further specify allowances for tiering during reevaluation; agencies remain responsible for ensuring the validity of reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and notice on reevaluation are context-dependent
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ declines to require that five-year reevaluations be subject to public comment or public notice as a blanket rule; some reevaluations may be simple and not require public comment while others may warrant public engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reevaluation reveals invalid assumptions or triggers supplementation criteria (§1502.9(d)), agencies must conduct supplemental analysis and public engagement as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference must include brief explanation of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must briefly explain the relevance of any material incorporated by reference into an environmental document in addition to summarizing the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explanation is intended to be concise (often a sentence) and improve transparency for decision makers and the public; CEQ expects agencies to integrate relevance explanation into the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material incorporated by reference must be reasonably available for public review throughout the comment/review period
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall not incorporate by reference material that is not reasonably available for public review; CEQ changes regulatory language to require availability 'throughout' the public comment or review period and uses 'review' rather than 'inspection.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies generally should make material available electronically or online but may provide physical copies in limited circumstances; proprietary data not available for review cannot be incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide digital references/hyperlinks and use publicly accessible websites as an example
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ encourages agencies to provide digital references, such as hyperlinks, to incorporated material or otherwise indicate how the public can access the material for review; a publicly accessible website is an example mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds this encouragement to improve transparency and accessibility; agencies may in future get additional eNEPA guidance on formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: No separate obligation to flag outdated/disputed incorporated material; disclose assumptions under other sections
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ declines to require agencies to separately disclose if cited material is outdated, disputed, or not fully proven; agencies already must disclose relevant assumptions or limitations under §1506.6 and §1502.21 for EISs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding a distinct requirement for incorporated material could create confusion; agencies should rely on existing obligations to disclose limitations and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference cannot circumvent public engagement and section 107(c) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference is a tool for efficiency but cannot be used to circumvent NEPA's public engagement, public comment, access, and transparency requirements, including the requirement to request public comment on relevant analyses for EISs under section 107(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ enforces the longstanding prohibition against incorporating material that is not reasonably available for review and recalls statutory comment obligations.
